headline: Trained at hospital A, frozen, then tested once at hospital B.
finding: The official utility score fell from 0.368 at hospital A dev to 0.238 at hospital B. At hospital B the model alerted by onset on 486 of 1142 sepsis patients (43%, against 62% at A dev) and missed 656. It raised a false alarm on 1358 of 18858 patients who never developed sepsis (7.2%, against the 15% budget set at hospital A).

two_hospitals.caption: The threshold was set once on hospital A dev at a 15% alert budget and never changed. Gray ranges are 95% ranges from a bootstrap that resamples patients 1,000 times. Hospital A dev is 4,068 patients the model did not train on. Hospital B is 20,000 patients from a different hospital, scored once.

models.caption: Each model's threshold was set on hospital A dev at the same 15% budget, then applied unchanged to hospital B. The gap between M2 and M3 shows how much the model leans on what was measured and when. That is a care pattern, not a cause.

travel_attempts.caption: The two adjustments use hospital B's measurements and scores but never its sepsis labels. They were planned before the hospital B run and are reported whether or not they helped.

prediction_box:
